3. Data Sources

Observed Data

The September historical time series is based on monthly average sea ice extent data provided by the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC). NSIDC’s data are derived from satellite imagery collected and processed by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC). This is the same source featured in Figure 1 of EPA’s Arctic Sea Ice indicator.

Model Outputs

This pairing presents outputs from 16 global climate models (GCMs) within the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) suite. Specific runs are noted in parentheses:

  • ACCESS-CM2 (r1i1p1f1)
  • ACCESS-ESM1-5 (r1i1p1f1)
  • BCC-CSM2-MR (r1i1p1f1)
  • CanESM5 (r1i1p1f1)
  • EC-Earth3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • FGOALS-g3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • GFDL-ESM4 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM4-8 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM5-0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • IPSL-CM6A-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MIROC6 (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-HR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MRI-ESM2-0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-LM (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-MM (r1i1p1f1)

Specifically, this analysis uses the “siconc” variable, which represents the percentage of each grid cell covered by sea ice.

4. Data Availability

Observed Data

The historical time series is based on monthly average sea ice extent data provided by NSIDC. NSIDC’s data are derived from satellite imagery collected and processed by NASA GSFC.

Model Outputs

CMIP6 monthly climate model outputs were retrieved from the publicly available CMIP6 data archive hosted by the Earth System Grid Federation. The overall technical documentation for this effort identifies the organizational ownership and direct source links for each of the individual models.
